title: Why the sky is blue, not white

scenes.text: Sunlight is white. So why is the sky blue?
Sunlight contains every color, mixed into white.
When it hits the air, tiny nitrogen and oxygen molecules scatter it.
Short blue waves scatter far more than long red ones, about five times more.
So blue light bounces all over the sky and reaches your eyes from every direction.
At sunset, light crosses much more air. The blue scatters away, leaving reds and oranges.
